CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  2

  A 10% CONTINGENCY ($36,080), FOR A TOTAL CONTRACT
  AUTHORIZATION OF $396,880, SUBJECT TO APPROVAL AS TO FORM BY
  THE CITY ATTORNEY.

  AYES:  Brown Schachter, Huff, Schmitz, Stegura, Zerunyan
  ABSENT:  None

B.  PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION ACTION ITEM: PENINSULA HOLIDAY
  PARADE MANAGEMENT SERVICES AGREEMENT

  Recommendation: That the City Council: 1) Approve changing the date of this year’s
  parade to December 12, 2026; and 2) Authorize the City Manager to sign the attached
  Agreement with Upbeat Parade Productions, LLC., to provide parade management
  services for the Peninsula Holiday Parade of Lights on December 12, 2026, approved
  as to the satisfaction of the City Attorney.

Community Services Supervisor Pinuelas provided a staff report (as per the agenda
material).

COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA asked how the proposed contractor’s cost compared to the
previous year. Supervisor Pinuelas responded that the new contractor is more costly but
specializes in parades and comes highly recommended, and stated that staff will pursue
additional sponsorships and work with the subcommittee and contractor to identify other cost-
saving opportunities.  .

COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF asked for clarification regarding the City’s responsibility for trophy
costs and the increase in the contractor’s cost. Staff confirmed that the City has traditionally
paid for trophies and will continue working directly with the same trophy vendor. Staff also
clarified that the parade contractor’s cost increased from approximately $15,000 last year to
$30,000 this year.

Staff reported conducting extensive outreach to identify alternative parade vendors, but
recommended selecting a contractor that specializes in parades due to the event’s specific
needs. Staff also noted increased efforts to secure sponsorships, including outreach through
the Chamber of Commerce and participation in an upcoming business expo.

Public comment was invited in-person in the Council Chamber, via email and via eComment.
No public testimony was received.

  COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER
  SCHMITZ, TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  1) APPROVE CHANGING THE DATE OF THIS YEAR’S PARADE TO
  DECEMBER 12, 2026; AND 2) AUTHORIZE THE CITY MANAGER TO SIGN
  THE ATTACHED AGREEMENT WITH UPBEAT PARADE PRODUCTIONS,
  LLC., TO PROVIDE PARADE MANAGEMENT SERVICES FOR THE
  PENINSULA HOLIDAY PARADE OF LIGHTS ON DECEMBER 12, 2026,
  APPROVED AS TO THE SATISFACTION OF THE CITY ATTORNEY.

  AYES:  Brown Schachter, Huff, Schmitz, Stegura, Zerunyan
  ABSENT:  None

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  3
AUGUST 25, 2026
 C.  PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION ACTION ITEM: SPECIAL EVENT PERMIT
  PROPOSAL - SOUTH COAST BOTANIC GARDEN OVERFLOW PARKING FOR
  UPCOMING EVENTS

  Recommendation: That the City Council approve the South Coast Botanic Garden’s
  request for after-hours use of Ernie Howlett Park for overflow parking associated with
  special events at the Garden on select dates from September 2026 through January
  2027, subject to the conditions and fees outlined in the attached report.

Community Services Supervisor Pinuelas provided a staff report (as per the agenda
material).

In response to COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF, Supervisor Pinuelas explained that the proposal is
for a new type of multi-day, after-hours event, unlike the City’s typical special events. Staff
addressed potential noise and neighborhood impacts with the organizer, including trained
parking staff, signage, attendee reminders, and shuttle service from Ernie Howlett Park. She
also noted staff will conduct an on-site review and regularly check in with the organizer to
promptly address any concerns or complaints.

Discussion ensued regarding the proposed after-hours event schedule, potential impacts on
regular park and equestrian use, and noise concerns for surrounding neighborhoods. South
Coast Botanic Garden Director Claire Griswold described their experience with similar events
and the sound-monitoring and mitigation measures in place to address potential concerns.

MAYOR ZERUNYAN asked about responsibility for opening and closing the park gate and
raised concerns regarding pedestrian safety and traffic control. Staff explained that Garden
staff would be trained to manage the gate, restrict access to event attendees, and ensure
attendees use the shuttle rather than cross Hawthorne Boulevard on foot. Staff also indicated
that traffic control needs would be evaluated with the Public Works Department, with
coordination with the Sheriff’s Department also discussed.

Public comment was invited in-person in the Council Chamber, via email and via eComment.
No public testimony was received.

  COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER
  STEGURA, TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  APPROVE THE SOUTH COAST BOTANIC GARDEN’S REQUEST FOR
  AFTER-HOURS USE OF ERNIE HOWLETT PARK FOR OVERFLOW
  PARKING ASSOCIATED WITH SPECIAL EVENTS AT THE GARDEN ON
  SELECT DATES FROM SEPTEMBER 2026 THROUGH JANUARY 2027,
  SUBJECT TO THE CONDITIONS AND FEES OUTLINED IN THE ATTACHED
  REPORT.

  AYES:  Brown Schachter, Huff, Schmitz, Stegura, Zerunyan
  ABSENT:  None

D.  LETTER OF OPPOSITION TO ASSEMBLY BILL 1751 (QUIRK-SILVA): MISSING
  MIDDLE TOWNHOME OWNERSHIP ACT

  Recommendation: That the City Council authorize the Mayor to sign the letter of
  opposition to AB 1751 (Quirk-Silva) - Missing Middle Townhome Ownership Act.

Assistant City Manager Slawson provided a staff report (as per the agenda material).

COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA expressed support for the letter of opposition, citing concerns
that the legislation applies a one-size-fits-all approach to cities and limits local discretion over
housing density and infrastructure considerations.

COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF noted the strong opposition to the legislation among cities in the
Los Angeles County Division.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  4
AUGUST 25, 2026
 Public comment was invited in-person in the Council Chamber, via email and via eComment.
No public testimony was received.

  MAYOR PRO TEM SCHACHTER moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER
  STEGURA, TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  AUTHORIZE THE MAYOR TO SIGN THE LETTER OF OPPOSITION TO AB
  1751 (QUIRK-SILVA) - MISSING MIDDLE TOWNHOME OWNERSHIP ACT.

  AYES:  Brown Schachter, Huff, Schmitz, Stegura, Zerunyan
  ABSENT:  None

9.  OLD BUSINESS

A.  REVISED MEMORANDUM OF UNDERSTANDING BETWEEN THE CITY OF
  ROLLING HILLS ESTATES AND CITIES OF LOMITA, RANCHO PALOS VERDES,
  AND ROLLING HILLS RELATING TO PROCUREMENT OF UNMANNED AERIAL
  SYSTEM (UAS) DRONES FOR THE LOMITA SHERIFF’S STATION

  Recommendation: That the City Council approve the revised Memorandum of
  Understanding between the City of Rolling Hills Estates and cities of Lomita, Rancho
  Palos Verdes, and Rolling Hills relating to the procurement of drones for the Lomita
  Sheriff’s Station.

Assistant to the City Manager Slawson provided a staff report (as per the agenda material).

COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA expressed support for the changes, stating that they provide
protections for the City and neighboring cities, and expressed pride in the City’s participation
in funding the drones for the Lomita Sheriff’s Station.

COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ expressed confidence in the Lomita Sheriff’s Station’s
thoughtful and professional use of technology, including ALPR systems, and stated that she
expects the drone technology to be utilized with the same care and professionalism.

COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF expressed support for the drone technology, noting that it could
provide a safer and quieter alternative to helicopters in addressing crime in the community.

Public comment was invited in-person in the Council Chamber, via email and via eComment.
Public testimony was received from resident Tony Trutanich who expressed some concerns
about the use of the drones.

In response to public comments, Los Angeles County Sheriff Deputy Tina McCoy clarified that
drones would be deployed and record only at or near specific incidents, rather than conduct
continuous surveillance while in flight. She confirmed that deployment records would be subject
to public disclosure through the Sheriff’s Department, the drones would carry identifying
Sheriff’s Department markings and comply with FAA requirements, and deployments would be
incident-driven rather than used for random or constant surveillance.

  MAYOR PRO TEM SCHACHTER moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER
  STEGURA, TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  APPROVE THE REVISED MEMORANDUM OF UNDERSTANDING
  BETWEEN THE CITY OF ROLLING HILLS ESTATES AND THE CITIES OF
  LOMITA, RANCHO PALOS VERDES, AND ROLLING HILLS RELATING TO
  THE PROCUREMENT OF DRONES FOR THE LOMITA SHERIFF’S STATION.

  AYES:  Brown Schachter, Huff, Schmitz, Stegura, Zerunyan
  ABSENT:  None
